meta.name: Planeta Tierra
meta.description: Aclamada serie de documentales creada por la BBC que nos muestra, en 11 episodios escritos por el prestigioso naturalista David Attenborough, la belleza de nuestro enorme planeta con imágenes nunca antes vistas.

videos.title: De polo a polo
videos.overview: Un recorrido por el mundo que analiza los comportamientos de los animales y revela los efectos del cambio climático en sus entornos.

videos.title: Montañas
videos.overview: Un recorrido por las principales cadenas montañosas del mundo y los hábitats que estas crean.

videos.title: Agua Dulce
videos.overview: Aunque representa apenas el 3 % del agua de la Tierra, el agua dulce desempeña un papel importante en el clima y la erosión del planeta. Es sumamente importante para toda la vida silvestre no marina, que bebe agua dulce y nada, se reproduce y caza en ella. Sus hábitats, como los ríos, los lagos y los pantanos, están repletos de especies acuáticas y de otro tipo, a menudo adaptadas a la vida «húmeda».

videos.title: Las Cuevas
videos.overview: Aunque a menudo se pasan por alto, las cuevas son hábitats extraordinarios con una fauna singular. Explora las estructuras creadas en el interior de la tierra, así como las adaptaciones que los animales han desarrollado para prosperar en estos entornos.

videos.title: Los Desiertos
videos.overview: A pesar de la falta de lluvia, los desiertos son los ecosistemas más variados que existen. De hecho, alrededor del treinta por ciento de la superficie terrestre está cubierta por desiertos. Explora las condiciones únicas que se dan en los desiertos, así como los mecanismos de supervivencia que han desarrollado los animales que los habitan.

videos.title: Mundos de hielo
videos.overview: Descubre cómo es la vida en los rincones más hostiles del planeta explorando el terreno, las estaciones y la fauna del Ártico y la Antártida.

videos.title: Llanuras
videos.overview: Este episodio aborda la sabana, la estepa, la tundra y la pradera, y analiza la importancia y la resiliencia de los pastos en estos ecosistemas sin árboles. Sus vastas extensiones albergan la mayor concentración de vida animal. En la sabana africana, la cámara capta un enjambre de 1.5 mil millones de queleas de pico rojo, la bandada de aves más grande jamás filmada.

videos.title: Selvas
videos.overview: Las selvas cubren aproximadamente el tres por ciento de nuestro planeta, pero albergan el cincuenta por ciento de las especies del mundo. Descubre la inmensa variedad de flora y fauna que habita en estas zonas únicas.

videos.title: Bajios
videos.overview: Un recorrido por las aguas poco profundas de la Tierra, desde los arrecifes de coral hasta los bosques de algas marinas y más allá.

videos.title: Bosques
videos.overview: Los árboles son los organismos más grandes de la Tierra y también se encuentran entre los habitantes más antiguos del planeta. Los bosques estacionales (a diferencia de la selva tropical) son los hábitats terrestres más extensos. Un tercio de todos los árboles crece en la interminable taiga del norte ártico. América del Norte cuenta con bosques que incluyen las secuoyas de California, los árboles más grandes de la Tierra. Allí y en otros lugares, su enorme capacidad de fotosíntesis y la sombra que proporcionan rigen un ciclo estacional de vida en el que participan innumerables especies de plantas y animales.

videos.title: Oceano ancho y profundo
videos.overview: Una exploración de los reinos más profundos y oscuros del océano, que abarca innumerables especies hasta una profundidad de 2,000 metros.

videos.title: Diaries - Eye in the Sky
videos.overview: Using the unique overhead heli-gimble camera the crew set out to film a pack of African wild dogs hunting in the Okavango Delta. It came down to the final hour of the final day of filming before they got the shot they wanted.

videos.title: Diaries - Snow Leopard Quest
videos.overview: Over the course of three years the Planet Earth team tried to film the elusive Snow Leopard deep in the mountains of Pakistan. Their patience was eventually rewarded with the world's first footage of a Snow Leopard hunting.

videos.title: Diaries - Diving with Piranhas
videos.overview: Cameraman Peter Scoones is on a mission to film Piranha in the wetlands of Brazil. They are considered the most dangerous freshwater fish, but prove difficult to track down, until Peter finally finds himself immersed in a feeding frenzy.

videos.title: Diaries - Into the Abyss
videos.overview: The team spend a month amongst an enormous mound of bat guano in Gomantong Cave as they film the hundreds of thousands of cockroaches and other inhabitants that live there. The amazing Lechuguilla Cave of New Mexico provides a whole other set of challenges.

videos.title: Diaries - Wild Camel Chase
videos.overview: The Gobi desert is home to the last truly wild Bactrian camels and their fear of humans makes them extremely difficult to capture on film. After weeks of trying the crew were becoming frustrated, but their expert local tracker wouldn't let them down.

videos.title: Diaries - Alive in the Freezer
videos.overview: Cameraman Wade Fairley braved temperatures of minus 50C and near hurricane force winds as he filmed a breeding colony of 20,000 emperor penguins in the Antarctic. At the other end of the Earth on a Norwegian island, cameraman Doug Allan and assistant Jason Roberts get a bit closer to a polar bear than they bargained for.

videos.title: Diaries - Shot in the Dark
videos.overview: Lions hunting elephants has only ever been seen by a handful of people, so the crew were up against it when trying to film this rare behaviour. Using infrared technology they were able to track a pride of lions through the African night, but when they finally got the shots they wanted it was a saddening experience for all.

videos.title: Diaries - Trouble in Paradise
videos.overview: It took the Planet Earth team over eight weeks in the field to film less than 15 minutes of footage of the beautiful but seldom seen Birds of Paradise in the highlands of Papua New Guinea. Behind the scenes cameraman Paul Stewart endured hundreds of hours alone cramped inside a small filming hide, going stir crazy when old songs come back to haunt him.

videos.title: Diaries - Shark Quest
videos.overview: Great white sharks capture their slippery seal prey by rocketing out of the depths and delivering a massive hit at the surface. To record a breach like this in ultra slow motion, which in real-time lasts just a second, was a supreme challenge for cameraman Simon King.

videos.title: Diaries - Ocean Wanderers
videos.overview: The camera team of Doug Anderson and Rick Rosenthal were determined to film oceanic whitetip sharks without a cage, relying only on observation, nerves and experience to dictate how long they stayed underwater in their company. The powerful sharks were initially shy of the dive team but, as more sharks arrived, they became bolder - their behaviour changing to that of the hunter.

videos.title: The Future: Saving Species
videos.overview: Many of the animals featured in the Planet Earth series are endangered so do we face an extinction crisis? Saving Species asks the experts if there really is a problem, looks at the reasons behind the declining numbers of particular animals and questions how we choose which species we want to conserve.

videos.title: The Future: Into the Wilderness
videos.overview: Pollution, climate change and a growing human population are all putting pressure on Earth's wildernesses including the Bialowieza forest, the Gobi Desert and the Arctic tundra. So how much of the planet is still wilderness? And why should we care? Into the Wilderness explores why these uninhabited expanses are important for our survival as well as that of all creatures on the planet.

videos.title: The Future: Living Together
videos.overview: This history of conservation throws up some interesting ideas as we look to the future of an ever more populated planet. How can conservation fit into this new world driven by economics and development? Living Together looks at the challenges facing conservation in the 21st century and looks at the role of religion in piloting a moral and ethical approach to the world we live in.

videos.title: The Making of Planet Earth
videos.overview: The making of the sprawling, ambitious series is documented.

videos.title: Desert Lions
videos.overview: Originally aired under BBC Natural World Collection. Many years ago lions thrived in the deserts of Namibia's Skeleton Coast, until they were exterminated by man. Six years ago maverick biologist Flip Stander discovered a tiny remnant population alive and well in nearby mountains, and started to study them. Their numbers have grown and they are now returning to the desert in increasing numbers. But if these lions are to continue roaming here, Flip will have to persuade local people that these lions are worth more alive than dead.

videos.title: Snow Leopard: Beyond the Myth
videos.overview: Originally aired under BBC Natural World Collection. The BBC Natural History Unit explores a secret cave deep in the mountains of Pakistan where generations of snow leopards return each year to raise their young.

videos.title: Great Planet Earth Moments

videos.title: Secrets of the Maya Underworld
videos.overview: The freshwater pools that dot Mexico's Yucatan peninsula were believed by the Mayans to be portals to the underworld. For the first time ever, the BBC Natural History Unit explores this incredible, labyrinthine system of underground rivers.

videos.title: Elephant Nomads of the Namib Desert
videos.overview: Follow the struggle for survival of two female elephants trying to raise their young in one of the harshest climates on Earth.

videos.title: To the Ends of the Earth
